A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WUKONG framework. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–G are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative comparisons, ablations and qualitative morphing results, including Headspace and SHREC07 evaluations in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains the original quantitative comparisons, ablations and qualitative results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The generator, Wasserstein barycenter interpolation, sequential initialization and similarity-threshold texture selection remain unchanged. Section 3.4 explains the two texture modes more explicitly, but both were already illustrated in v1 Figures 1–2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate image- and text-conditioned morphing, cross-category object transitions, Headspace face scans and SHREC07 shape morphing. The additional examples in Appendix E are also retained unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains DiffMorpher, AID, MV-Adapter, Luma, MorphFlow and 3DRM. Appendix D retains MapTree, BIM, SmoothShells, NeuroMorph and SRIF, with unchanged membership in the corresponding comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation procedures, metrics and backbone configurations are unchanged. Section 4 retains 25 sampling steps per flow, guidance strength 3 and J = 6; the appendix evaluation protocols also match.

E4.justification: Figures 6–8 and Tables 2–5 retain the same interpolation, initialization, texture-selection, backbone and threshold analyses. Revised explanations and relocated figures do not introduce or remove ablation evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point-estimate tables without experimental run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–7 and the qualitative result images are unchanged. For example, WUKONG retains FID 4.01 and PPL 2.91 in Table 1 and FID 3.97 on Headspace in Table 6.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12 and Appendix C's continuity, convexity, optimality and inference-speed arguments retain their mathematical content. Explicitly identifying alpha as a discrete interpolation index restates the existing sequence definition.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution (iii) reframe selective interpolation from remedying texture degradation and oversmoothing to enabling identity-preserving texture control alongside global transitions. The training-free framework, principal algorithmic contributions and superiority claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 adds an explanation that imposing static source tokens on deforming geometry causes texture–geometry misalignment. It also distinguishes smooth default transitions from deliberate source-identity preservation, replacing the earlier emphasis on undesirable averaging. Appendix G's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The solver, optimization settings, encoders, architecture descriptions, A100 hardware, approximately 30-second generation time and project-page information are retained. Adding the word GPU and clarifying behavior already depicted in Figure 2 do not add substantive reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and bibliography retain the same cited works and positioning relative to existing morphing and generation methods. No references are added or removed.

P1.justification: Localized revisions clarify the abstract, introduction and Section 3.4, shorten the shape-ablation discussion, and correct grammar and spelling. The overall section and appendix organization is unchanged.

P2.justification: Existing displays are repositioned: Table 1 moves from page 6 to 7, Figure 4 from page 7 to 8, and Figures 6–7 from page 8 to 9. Captions clarify textured versus texture-controlled morphing. The underlying illustrations and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 more clearly explains the two texture modes already illustrated in v1 and why fixed source tokens can misalign with changing geometry (Section 3.4). Together with tighter ablation prose and language corrections, this provides a limited improvement in clarity. The experimental evidence and mathematical support remain unchanged.
